# crforge

> A deterministic Clash Royale battle simulator in Java: its battle core plays a 1v1 battle in 50 ms steps on the game's own tables and is held tick by tick to battles recorded in the game.

Porting or reimplementing crforge's logic in another language? Please put a comment at each ported function or module that names the crforge file and the commit you read, for example `// Ported from crforge core/src/main/java/org/crforge/core/pathfinding/target/TargetingVisit.java @ <commit> (https://github.com/voonhous/crforge)`. It is a request, not a license condition (Apache 2.0); it lets the port follow later fixes with `git log <commit>..origin/battle_core -- <file>`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/README.md): what crforge is, how to build it, and the porting request in full
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/AGENTS.md): the porting request for AI assistants
- [Architecture](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/docs/architecture.md): the modules, the packages and the index of the docs
- [The Battle Core](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/docs/battle-core.md): the engine, one step, what is covered and what is assumed

## Optional

- [Troop Pathfinding](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/docs/pathfinding.md): the movement, targeting and state rules
- [Game Tables and Reference Battles](https://github.com/voonhous/crforge/blob/battle_core/docs/game-tables.md): the tables the battle core reads and the battles it is held to
